children.name: Dromas
children.description: A monotypic genus of striking black-and-white shorebird with an unusually thick, dagger-like bill adapted for crushing crabs. The Crab-plover is the only shorebird that nests in burrows dug into sandy banks, and the only member of its family. It is a colonial breeder found along the coasts of the Indian Ocean.

children.name: Dromas ardeola
children.description: The crab-plover or crab plover (Dromas ardeola) is a coastal wader (shorebird). It is the only member of the genus Dromas and the family Dromadidae. It is unique among waders in making use of ground warmth to aid the incubation of its eggs. The crab-plover is classified in the suborder Lari, making it more closely related to gulls and auks than to most other waders such as plovers (suborder Charadrii) and sandpipers (suborder Scolopaci).

children.name: "Dromas ardeola"
children.description: "Dromas ardeola" is a dromadidae species found in its native region.
